text: Sensory processing depends on interactions between neural circuits that convey and regulate information across cortical and subcortical networks. Classical frameworks distinguish driving inputs, which transmit sensory content via suprathreshold activation, from modulatory inputs, which alter neuronal excitability without directly eliciting spiking. However, physiological signatures of these circuit types that generalize widely across distributed brain regions remain unclear.
source_label: Spectrotemporal signatures of driving- and modulatory circuits across cortical and subcortical networks
